sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: LocalAI runs open AI models on your own hardware behind an API that speaks the OpenAI and Anthropic formats. It covers chat, images, speech, video, embeddings and more, with a web interface for chats, agents and team projects.
sixtySeconds.problem: Cloud AI APIs send your data to third parties and charge per call. LocalAI lets apps built for the OpenAI or Anthropic APIs use models running on your own laptop or server instead, with your files staying on your machines.
whoFor: Developers who want a self-hosted OpenAI-compatible API
Teams keeping data on their own servers
Admins serving models to a group of users
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for one self-hosted API across text, vision, speech, images and video, with more than 80 backends and support for NVIDIA, AMD, Intel, Apple Silicon, Vulkan or CPU only.
requirements: Linux or macOS on Apple Silicon for the script; Docker anywhere
A GPU is optional; CPU only works
Disk space for models (the small Gemma example is 4.3 GB)

overview: Install with the script, which downloads the release binary and checks its checksum, or run the Docker image. Start the server with local-ai and open http://localhost:8080 to install models from the web UI, or start a model directly with local-ai run followed by a model name.

Models can come from the built-in gallery, Hugging Face, the Ollama registry or any OCI registry. LocalAI detects your GPU and downloads the matching backend; separate Docker images exist for NVIDIA CUDA 12 and 13, AMD ROCm, Intel oneAPI, Vulkan and NVIDIA Jetson.
On top of the API it offers chats with saved agents, MCP tools, projects, add-ons like Office and Sandbox, API key auth and user quotas, and a desktop app for macOS and Linux. It is MIT licensed.

Restart it with docker start -i local-ai.
Use the GPU image for your vendor, e.g. latest-gpu-nvidia-cuda-12 with --gpus all.
